plot.label: Population pyramid of Country P: the bars are widest at ages 0 to 4 and get shorter at every older age, a wide base and a narrow top
Population pyramid of Country Q: the bars are shortest at ages 0 to 4, widest at ages 45 to 59, and more women than men at ages 80 and over, a narrow base

items.q: Which phrase describes the shape of Country P’s pyramid?
options: Expansive: a wide base that narrows quickly
Constrictive: a base narrower than the middle bars of the pyramid
Stationary: nearly straight sides until old age
Top-heavy: more older people than children

why.correct: An expansive pyramid has a wide base and narrows quickly toward the top. It shows a young population with many children.
options: Right: the youngest bars are the longest and each older bar is shorter.
P’s base is its widest part.
P’s sides slope in steeply from the bottom.
P has far more children than older people.

items.q: Add the bars for ages 0 to 14 (both sexes) on Country P’s pyramid. To the nearest whole percent, what share of Country P’s people are under 15?

mistakes.why: You added only the male bars. The pyramid splits each age group into males (left) and females (right); add both sides.

why.correct: Add six bars, three male and three female: 7.7 + 6.9 + 6.1 + 7.4 + 6.7 + 5.9, which is about 41 percent.

items.q: What will Country P most likely need more of in the next 15 years?
options: Care homes and pensions for a growing share of retired people
Fewer teachers, because the number of children is falling
Schools, and then jobs for young adults
Workers from abroad to replace a shrinking workforce

why.correct: A wide base means many children. Over the next 15 years they move up the pyramid, first into schools and then into the job market.
options: P has very few people over 65; its needs are for the young.
the youngest bars are the longest, so the number of children is large.
Right: the many many young children will need schools, then work.
P’s workforce will grow as its many children reach working age.

items.q: Which cohort is the largest in Country Q?
options: Children aged 0 to 4
People aged 80 and over
Young adults aged 20 to 24
People aged 50 to 54

why.correct: A cohort is a group of people born in the same years. In Country Q the 50-54 cohort has the longest bars.
options: the 0-4 bars are the shortest in the pyramid.
the 80+ group is small, even though women outnumber men in it.
the 20-24 bars are shorter than the bars for ages 40 to 59.
Right: the 50-54 bars are the longest on both sides.

items.q: What does the narrow base of Country Q’s pyramid suggest?
options: Fewer babies are born each year than 50 years ago
Many young children are dying before they reach school age
Many families with babies have moved into Country Q from abroad
The population of Country Q will grow quickly in the next 20 years

why.correct: A base narrower than the middle bars is a constrictive pyramid. It shows that births have fallen: the cohorts born recently are smaller than those born decades ago.
options: Right: the youngest cohorts are smaller than those born half a century earlier.
the base narrows smoothly over many groups, the pattern of falling births.
that would widen the base, not narrow it.
few children now means fewer future parents, so growth slows.

items.q: In Country Q, women outnumber men in the 80 and over group. Which statement best explains this?
options: More girls than boys are born each year in most countries
On average, women live longer than men
Older women are counted twice in many censuses
Older men in Country Q have moved abroad in large numbers

why.correct: Women live longer than men on average in almost every country, so the sex ratio falls at older ages and the female side of the top bars is longer.
options: slightly more boys are usually born, about 105 for every 100 girls.
Right: more women survive to the oldest ages, so the female bar is longer.
there is no such counting rule.
the pyramid cannot show this, and men living shorter lives is the usual reason.

items.q: Which question can Country Q’s national pyramid NOT answer?
options: Whether children or adults aged 50 to 54 are more numerous in Country Q
Whether women outnumber men in the oldest group
Which cities in Country Q have the most older people
Which age group is the largest in Country Q

why.correct: A national pyramid describes the whole country’s age and sex structure. It cannot show where in the country each group lives, or why the pattern formed: those need data at another scale.
options: the bars show this: the 50-54 bars are longer.
the 80+ bars show more women than men.
Right: a national pyramid has no data on where people live inside the country.
the longest bars show the largest cohort.
The share of men compared with women in a population
The number of people for each square kilometer of land
A graph that shows a population by age and sex
A group of people born in the same years

why.correct: A cohort is a group born in the same period, such as everyone aged 20 to 24. Pyramids show one cohort per bar.
options: that is the sex ratio.
that is population density.
that is a population pyramid, which is made of cohorts.
Right: each bar of a pyramid is a cohort.

items.q: An invented country has 52 million males and 48 million females. What is its sex ratio, to the nearest whole number?

mistakes.why: You put females on top. The sex ratio is males per 100 females, so males go on top.
That is the share of males in the population (52 percent), not males per 100 females.

items.q: In Qatar, men aged 25 to 44 far outnumber women of the same ages (Qatar census, 2020). Which explanation fits this part of its pyramid?
options: Far more boys than girls were born in Qatar 30 years ago
Many men from other countries come to work there
Women in Qatar leave the country for work at age 25
Women in Qatar are not counted in its census data

why.correct: A large bulge of men of working age on the left side of a pyramid usually shows workers who moved in from other countries. In Qatar, most of them work in building and services.
options: births alone cannot make men outnumber women this much.
Right: a bulge of working-age men is the mark of labor migration.
there is no such large outflow of women.
Qatar’s census counts both men and women.

items.q: The baby boom in the United States lasted from 1946 to 1964. In a pyramid of the United States for 2020, where would the baby boomers appear?
options: As a wide band at ages 0 to 19
As a wide band at ages 30 to 44, the middle of the pyramid
As a wide band at ages 55 to 74
As a narrow band at ages 80 and over

why.correct: A cohort moves up the pyramid as it ages. A large birth cohort shows as a bulge that climbs about one bar every five years.
options: those are people born from 2001 to 2020.
those were born from 1976 to 1990.
Right: people born 1946 to 1964 were 56 to 74 years old in 2020.
the boomers were all younger than 75 in 2020.

items.q: A pyramid for State College, Pennsylvania, a town with a large university, has a huge bulge at ages 18 to 24. The pyramid for the whole United States does not. What does this show?
options: The United States is losing people aged 18 to 24 to other countries
State College has more babies than other towns in the country
The national data for the United States are wrong
Patterns at the local scale can differ from the national pattern

why.correct: Scale changes what a pyramid shows. A college town (local scale) has a bulge of students that the national pyramid hides.
options: the national pyramid shows no such loss, and the town gives no evidence of it.
the bulge is at ages 18 to 24, not at the base.
both can be right: the town pulls students from the whole country.
Right: students gather in one town, so the local pyramid has a bulge.

items.q: Which can you read directly from a population pyramid? Select all that apply.
options: The share of the population in each age group
Whether men or women are more numerous at each age
Where in the country older people live
Why births have fallen
How many people moved in last year

why.correct: A pyramid shows age structure (the share in each age group) and the sex ratio at each age. It does not show places, causes or yearly moves.
options: Right: each bar is a cohort’s share.
Right: compare the left and right bars.
A pyramid has no locations; that needs a map.
A pyramid shows that births fell, not why.
A pyramid shows age and sex, not yearly moves.

items.q: As a country’s birth rate falls over many decades, its pyramid changes shape. Put the shapes in order, from high birth rate to very low birth rate.

slips.why: A constrictive pyramid comes last: its base has shrunk below the middle bars. Straight sides (stationary) come first, when births have just leveled off.

why.correct: High births give a wide base (expansive). When births level off, the sides become nearly straight (stationary). When births fall below earlier levels, the base becomes narrower than the middle (constrictive).

items.q: Build an explanation of what a pyramid shape means for a named country.

specific.model: In Niger, the pyramid has a very wide base, with nearly half of the people under 15 (UN WPP 2024), so the country needs many more schools and, later, jobs.

place.label: Place
options: Niger
a poor country

why.1: name a real country; "a poor country" is vague and not a pyramid shape.

pattern.label: Shape
options: a very wide base, with nearly half of the people under 15
many people

why.1: "many people" is about size, not shape; describe the base.

effect.label: Effect and its link
options: the country needs many more schools and, later, jobs
the population is large

why.1: that repeats the data; an explanation names what the shape leads to.

why.correct: Name the place, describe the shape from the data, then link it to a future need.

items.q: A pyramid of a retirement town in Florida is widest at ages 65 to 79 and very narrow at ages 0 to 19. Which service will the town most likely need more of?
options: New primary schools for a large number of young children
Child care centers for working parents with babies
Playgrounds and youth sports fields
Health care for older residents

why.correct: A pyramid shows who lives in a place, which tells planners what services they need. A top-heavy local pyramid points to health care and services for older people.
options: the 0-19 bars are very narrow.
there are few young families in this town.
few children live in the town.
Right: a large share of people over 65 needs more doctors and clinics.
